extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent applicants, patent attorneys, and Patent Office officials (United States, 1836)
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules and procedural requirements for obtaining, correcting, extending, and enforcing patents under the U.S. Patent Act and its 1836 additions. Covers caveats, reissues, recordings, models, fees, defenses, remedies, office procedures, and evidentiary rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat filing (content and fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who has invented any new art, machine, or improvement and desires further time may file in the Patent Office a caveat setting forth the design and purpose thereof, and its principal and distinguishing characteristics, praying protection until he shall have matured his invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing requires payment of twenty dollars (which counts toward later patent duty if patent is taken out). Caveats are filed in the confidential archives and preserved in secrecy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat interference notice and response period
rubrics_metrics.description: If another person applies within one year for a patent that may in any respect interfere with a filed caveat, the Commissioner shall deposit the applicant's description, specifications, drawings, and model in the confidential archives and mail notice to the caveat filer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The caveat filer then has three months after receiving notice to file his description, specification, drawings, and model to avail himself of the caveat; if Commissioner deems specifications to interfere, like proceedings as in interfering applications may be had.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner opinions do not preclude judicial contest
rubrics_metrics.description: No opinion or decision of any board of examiners shall preclude any person interested in favor of or against the validity of any patent from contesting the same in any judicial court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative decisions are not binding on courts; parties retain right to litigate patent validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue for defective or insufficient specification (conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a patent is inoperative or invalid by reason of a defective or insufficient description or specification, or by claiming more than the patentee had right to claim, and the error arose by inadvertency, accident, or mistake without fraudulent intention, the Commissioner may, upon surrender of the patent and payment of fifteen dollars, issue a new patent to the inventor for the same invention for the residue of the unexpired term in accordance with the corrected description and specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue requires surrender of original patent and payment of $15; in case of death or assignment, executors/assignees have similar rights; reissued patent has same legal effect as though originally filed in corrected form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annexing subsequent improvements to an issued patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee desirous of adding the description and specification of any new improvement of the original invention, invented after the patent date, may proceed as in original applications and, on payment of fifteen dollars, have the same annexed to the original description and specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner shall certify on the margin of the annexed description the time of its being annexed and recorded; annexed material thereafter has the same legal effect as if embraced in the original specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courts' discretion to award enhanced damages
rubrics_metrics.description: In actions for damages for making, using, or selling a patented thing, courts may render judgment for any sum above the amount found by verdict as actual damages, not exceeding three times that amount, according to the circumstances of the case, with costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhanced damages are discretionary and limited to treble actual damages; recovery by action on the case in courts of competent jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant may plead general issue and give notice of special defenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendant in an infringement action may plead the general issue and give in evidence this act and any special matter of which written notice may have been given to plaintiff or attorney thirty days before trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible evidence includes matters tending to prove the plaintiff's specification fails to contain whole truth, contains more than necessary to produce effect, concealment or addition made to deceive, or that plaintiff was not original inventor, or prior public description/use/sale, or surreptitious obtaining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific grounds of defense to be pleaded/proved
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendant may rely on proof that the specification does not contain the whole truth, contains more than necessary, concealment/addition intended to deceive, that the patentee was not original inventor or first discoverer of the thing or a substantial part claimed, that it was described in a public work prior, or had been in public use or on sale with patentee's consent prior to application, or that patentee surreptitiously or unjustly obtained the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If defendant relies on prior invention, knowledge, or use, he must state in his notice the names and places of residence of those he intends to prove possessed prior knowledge and where used; judgment for defendant when such defenses succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign prior knowledge proviso (good faith applicant)
rubrics_metrics.description: If at time of application the patentee believed himself to be first inventor, the patent shall not be void because the invention had been before known or used in any foreign country, provided it had not been previously patented or described in any printed publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects honest belief in priority as to foreign prior use absent prior patent or printed description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication when plaintiff overclaims
rubrics_metrics.description: When plaintiff fails to sustain action because his specification or claim embraces more than he was first inventor of, but defendant used or violated any part truly and justly specified and claimed as new, the court may adjudge costs as just and equitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court has equitable discretion to apportion costs when partial rights are infringed despite overbroad claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for interfering patents or adverse examiner decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When there are two interfering patents or when an application is refused by examiners on ground of interference with an unexpired patent, any interested person may have remedy by bill in equity; courts may declare patents void in whole or in part or adjudge that an applicant is entitled to receive a patent for his invention according to priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudication in equity can order issuance of patent to successful applicant upon filing copy of adjudication and compliance with statutory requisitions; judgment affects only parties and those deriving title from them after rendition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal jurisdiction and injunction power
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions and suits arising under U.S. laws granting exclusive rights to inventors shall be originally cognizable in U.S. circuit courts (or district courts with circuit powers), which may grant injunctions according to equity principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals or writs of error from such judgments lie to the U.S. Supreme Court as in other circuit court judgments; courts may condition injunctions as they deem reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-term extension application procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee desiring extension beyond original term may apply in writing to the Commissioner setting forth grounds and pay $40; Commissioner shall publish notice in principal Washington papers and other proper papers and convene a board (Secretary of State, Commissioner, Solicitor of Treasury) to hear evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee must furnish under oath a written statement of the ascertained value of the invention and detailed receipts/expenditures. Extension granted only if board, with regard to public interest, determines it's just and proper because patentee (without neglect or fault) failed to obtain reasonable remuneration; extension length seven years from expiration of first term; no extension after expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office library provision
rubrics_metrics.description: A library of scientific works and periodicals, foreign and American, shall be provided for the use of the Patent Office to facilitate duty discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriation of $1500 from the patent fund; to be purchased under direction of Committee of the Library of Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and public display of models and specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner shall classify and arrange models, specimens of compositions, fabrics, and other manufactures (patented or unpatented) in rooms or galleries conducive to beneficial display and keep them open during suitable hours for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models and specimens to be preserved where necessary and displayed suitably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and re-recording of patents/assignments (pre-Dec 15, 1836)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons in possession of patents or assignments issued prior to December 15, 1836, may, without charge, present them to the Commissioner to be recorded anew in the Patent Office together with descriptions, specifications, claims, and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner must transcribe/copy into record books; where drawings were not originally annexed, a verified drawing may be transmitted and placed on file or copied; clerks of judicial courts must transmit authenticated copies; certified copies by Commissioner are prima facie evidence when recorded anew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies as prima facie evidence after re-recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of patents, records, and drawings certified by the Commissioner (or chief clerk in his absence) and recorded anew shall be prima facie evidence of the particulars of the invention and patent in U.S. courts where originals would be evidence, without proof of loss of originals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents or assignments prior to Dec 15 will not be received in evidence after June 1 unless recorded anew and drawing verified; written assignments also must be re-recorded anew to be received in evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: New patents for lost or destroyed originals (date and proof)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent was destroyed (e.g., Patent Office fire) or otherwise lost, the Commissioner, on application by patentee or interested person, must issue a new patent for the same invention bearing the date of the original patent, provided the applicant deposits a duplicate of the original model, drawings, and descriptions with specifications verified by oath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New patent shall be entered of record; copies of drawings and descriptions duly certified shall be admissible as evidence and protect rights only to the same extent as the original patent would have.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner duty to procure duplicates of valuable destroyed models
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner shall procure duplicates of the models destroyed by fire that were most valuable and necessary to facilitate discharge of duties and to protect public and patentees' rights, subject to reasonable expense and a total expenditure limit of $100,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A temporary board of Commissioners (Commissioner + two Presidential appointees) shall determine which models to obtain and the mode of obtaining them and may establish necessary regulations, terms, and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction/reissue and divisional patents (fee and duplicate model requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent is returned for correction and reissue and the patentee desires several patents for distinct parts, he must pay an additional sum ($30 for each additional patent) and, for patents made prior to Dec 15, deposit a verified duplicate of the model and drawing as originally invented before correction/reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No correction or reissue for patents prior to Dec 15 shall be made until duplicate model/drawing is deposited and verified by oath as required by the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: No addition of improvements to existing patents without duplicate model/drawing
rubrics_metrics.description: No addition of an improvement shall be made to any patent heretofore granted, nor any new patent for an improvement to the original inventor/assignee be made, nor any disclaimer admitted to record, until a verified duplicate model and drawing of the thing originally invented is deposited in the Patent Office if the Commissioner requires it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner may require duplicate models/drawings; compliance preserves evidentiary and patent-granting integrity after loss or destruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation for models and drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions of compensation for models and drawings (e.g., duplicates obtained) shall be subject to the judgment and decision of the temporary Commissioners created for that purpose, under prescribed limitations and restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation determinations are administrative and constrained by the act's limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents may be issued to assignees with conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any patent hereafter to be issued may be made and issued to the assignee(s) of the inventor, the assignment being first entered of record and the application being duly made and the specification sworn to by the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must furnish duplicate drawings where case admits; one drawing to be deposited in the office and the other annexed to the patent and considered part of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer procedure for overbroad claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee (or his administrators, executors, assigns) who has, through inadvertence, accident, or mistake, made his specification or claim too broad may make a disclaimer in writing of such parts as he does not claim, stating the extent of his interest; it must be attested by witnesses and recorded in the Patent Office on payment of ten dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclaimer becomes part of the original specification to the extent of the interest of the disclaimant and those claiming under him; it does not affect any action pending at the time except as to unreasonable neglect or delay in filing the disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications to add newly discovered improvements are reviewed like originals
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to add a newly discovered improvement to an existing patent, or patents returned for correction/reissue, shall have their specifications and claims subject to revision and restriction in the same manner as original applications; Commissioner will not add the improvement or grant reissue until applicant has entered disclaimer or altered specification/claim per Commissioner's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant dissatisfied with Commissioner's decision has same remedies and privileges as in original applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent validity for bona fide part when overclaiming (inadvertence)
rubrics_metrics.description: When, by mistake or inadvertence and without intent to defraud, a patentee has claimed as original inventor a material or substantial part of the thing patented of which he was not the first inventor, the patent shall be deemed good and valid for so much of the invention as shall be truly and bona fide his own, provided that part is material, substantial, and definitively distinguishable from the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patentee (or successors) may maintain suit for infringement of the bona fide part, but to recover costs they must have entered at the Patent Office a disclaimer of the parts claimed without right prior to commencement of the suit; unreasonable delay in filing the disclaimer forfeits the benefits of this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents to receive and forward models
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may appoint agents (not exceeding twenty) in principal cities or towns to receive and forward to the Patent Office models, specimens, and manufactures intended for patenting or deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transportation of such items is chargeable to the patent fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing and compensation for examining and copying clerks
rubrics_metrics.description: Two examining clerks shall be appointed (each salary $1500), and an additional copying clerk (salary $800); the Commissioner may employ temporary clerks as necessary, who shall receive up to seven cents per 100-word page for copying and reasonable compensation for drawings and comparing records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision authorizes temporary staff to execute copying, drafting, and comparing records with originals; Commissioner sets compensation as agreed or prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund to foreign applicants rejected for want of novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: If a foreigner's application is rejected and withdrawn for want of novelty, the Commissioner's certificate of rejection is sufficient warrant for the Treasurer to refund two-thirds of the duty paid for the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative certificate used to effect partial refund to foreign applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmation may substitute for oath
rubrics_metrics.description: In all cases where an oath is required by the act, if the person required is conscientiously scrupulous of taking an oath, an affirmation may be substituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits non-oath affirmations for conscientious objectors.
